baslik: Hail Killed Both Engines and the Jet Landed on a Highway
sonuc: made a forced landing on a Georgia highway
tetik: flying into a severe thunderstorm cell
mekanizma: massive water and hail ingestion stalling and damaging both engine compressors
ders: the case sharpened guidance on avoiding rather than penetrating severe storms
yanilgi: The engines didn't simply fail. They swallowed so much hail and water that their compressors were wrecked.
tartisma: One board member blamed the decision to fly into the storm. Should radar ever be used to fly through storms?
basliklar: Why Southern Airways Flight 242 Lost Both Engines
The Storm That Killed Both Engines
soru: Avoid the storm, or cross it?
sahneler: A DC-9 with no working engines tried to land on a Georgia highway.
It crashed into roadside buildings, and seventy two people were killed.
The crew had flown into a severe thunderstorm.
Hail was so intense it broke the windshield.
Both engines swallowed massive amounts of water and hail.
Their compressors were wrecked, and both flamed out.
One board member blamed the decision to fly into the storm.
It remains Georgia's deadliest air crash.

baslik: The Wind Shear Warning That Went to the Wrong Frequency
sonuc: crashed into trees and a house near Charlotte
tetik: a microburst during a go-around in a thunderstorm
mekanizma: microburst wind shear on approach, with alerts that came late or on another frequency
ders: wind shear detection and crew recognition training were improved
yanilgi: A wind shear warning was issued. It went out on a frequency the crew wasn't listening to.
tartisma: An alert system software error also delayed its warning. How many layers must fail at once?
basliklar: Why USAir Flight 1016 Crashed
The Warning the Crew Never Heard
sahneler: A DC-9 crashed into trees and a house near Charlotte airport.
It burst into flames, and thirty seven people were killed.
A thunderstorm sat over the airport.
The tower issued a wind shear warning, but on a different frequency.
On final approach, a microburst hit the jet.
The crew tried to go around, but the plane kept sinking.
An alert system error also delayed its warning.
Wind shear detection and crew training were improved.

baslik: Twenty-Seven Minutes of Snow After De-icing
sonuc: crashed on take-off in a Denver snowstorm
tetik: wing contamination after a long delay since de-icing
mekanizma: ice on the upper wing combined with an over-rapid rotation causing a stall on lift-off
ders: rules for newly qualified crews and de-icing hold-over times were tightened
yanilgi: The jet was de-iced. Too much time passed before take-off, and ice formed again.
tartisma: Both pilots were inexperienced on the jet. Should two new pilots ever fly together?
basliklar: Why Continental Flight 1713 Crashed
The Ice That Came Back After De-icing
sahneler: A DC-9 rolled over and crashed on take-off in a Denver snowstorm.
It broke apart on the runway, and twenty five passengers and three crew were killed.
The jet had been de-iced before departure.
Then it waited twenty seven minutes for take-off.
Snow and ice built up on the wings again.
The first officer rotated too fast, and the left wing stalled.
Both pilots were inexperienced on the DC-9.
Rules for newly qualified crews were tightened.

baslik: A Fighter Jet and an Airliner Met Over the Mountains
sonuc: collided with a military jet over the San Gabriel Mountains
tetik: a fighter flying under visual rules through a civilian corridor
mekanizma: midair collision where neither crew saw the other in time and the fighter wasn't under radar control
ders: military jets were required to contact civilian controllers in civil airspace
yanilgi: The skies weren't crowded. Neither crew saw the other in time.
tartisma: Military and civilian traffic shared the same sky with different rules. Who should own the airspace?
basliklar: Why Hughes Airwest Flight 706 Collided With a Fighter
The Midair Collision Over the San Gabriels
sahneler: Over the San Gabriel Mountains, an airliner and a Marine fighter collided.
Both crashed, killing all forty nine aboard the DC-9 and the fighter's pilot.
The fighter was flying under visual flight rules.
It wasn't in contact with civilian controllers.
The airliner was climbing out of Los Angeles.
Neither crew saw the other in time.
The fighter's radar officer ejected and survived.
Military jets were then required to contact civilian controllers.

baslik: The Small Talk That Created the Sterile Cockpit Rule
sonuc: crashed short of the runway at Charlotte
tetik: a crew distracted by idle conversation during approach
mekanizma: descent below safe altitude while the crew failed to monitor instruments
ders: the sterile cockpit rule banned non-essential talk during critical phases
yanilgi: Nothing broke on the aircraft. The crew's attention drifted during the most critical minutes.
tartisma: A rule now bans casual talk below a set altitude. Can rules control attention?
basliklar: Why Eastern Flight 212 Crashed
The Conversation That Changed Cockpit Rules
sahneler: A DC-9 crashed in fog several miles short of the Charlotte runway.
It broke apart and burned, and seventy two of eighty two aboard were killed.
Nothing was wrong with the aircraft.
On approach, the crew talked about politics and cars.
Nobody watched the altitude closely.
The jet descended far below the safe height.
Investigators blamed a lack of attention.
It led to the sterile cockpit rule.

baslik: A Switch in the Wrong Mode and a Jet Hit a Seawall
sonuc: struck a seawall at Boston Logan
tetik: a flight director probably left in go-around mode
mekanizma: unstabilized approach in fog while the crew was preoccupied with misleading guidance
ders: stabilized approach and altitude call-out practices were reinforced
yanilgi: The instrument didn't fail. It was likely set to the wrong mode, and it absorbed the crew's attention.
tartisma: No altitude call-outs were made. Who should watch the altitude when automation confuses?
basliklar: Why Delta Flight 723 Hit the Seawall
The Flight Director in the Wrong Mode
hook: It was in the wrong mode
sahneler: In low cloud and fog, a DC-9 struck a seawall at Boston Logan.
It crashed and burned, killing all eighty nine people aboard.
The jet reached the outer marker too fast and too high.
Its flight director was likely switched into go-around mode.
The crew focused on its confusing guidance.
No one called out the altitude.
The jet passed decision height and kept descending.
Stabilized approach and altitude call-out practices were reinforced.

baslik: Hundreds of Coal Pillars Collapsed Like Dominoes
sonuc: collapsed underground, trapping hundreds of miners
tetik: undersized pillars left supporting a taller mined roof
mekanizma: cascading pillar failure as each collapse overloaded its neighbours
ders: South Africa introduced pillar design research and safety rules
yanilgi: The warning signs were visible. Miners who ran to the surface were ordered back underground.
tartisma: Miners were threatened with prison if they didn't return. Who can refuse unsafe work?
basliklar: Why the Coalbrook Mine Collapsed
The Pillars That Fell Like Dominoes
sahneler: Deep under South Africa, hundreds of coal pillars suddenly caved in.
Miners were trapped underground, and four hundred thirty seven died.
Pillars of coal were left to hold up the roof.
But mining had made the tunnels taller and the pillars thinner.
When a few failed, the load shifted to the next.
Miners felt a blast of wind and ran for the surface.
They were ordered back underground.
It pushed South Africa into pillar design research.

baslik: The River So Polluted It Kept Catching Fire
tetik: oil-soaked industrial debris on the water
mekanizma: industrial pollution leaving flammable oil and debris floating on the river
ders: it helped spur the Clean Water Act amendments and the EPA
yanilgi: The 1969 fire wasn't the worst. The river had caught fire at least 14 times.
tartisma: A small fire became a national symbol. Why do some disasters change laws and others don't?
basliklar: Why the Cuyahoga River Caught Fire
The River That Burned
sahneler: In Cleveland, the Cuyahoga River caught fire.
Suddenly flames spread across oily debris on the water.
Factories had dumped waste into it for decades.
Oil and debris floated on the surface.
The river had burned at least fourteen times.
This fire drew national attention.
It helped spark the modern environmental movement.
It helped spur the Clean Water Act amendments and the EPA.

baslik: The Fog That Killed Thousands in London
sonuc: blanketed London in toxic smog for five days
tetik: cold windless weather trapping coal smoke
mekanizma: an anticyclone and temperature inversion holding coal pollution over the city
ders: the Clean Air Act 1956 restricted coal smoke
yanilgi: It looked like ordinary London fog. Deaths ran far higher than first estimates.
tartisma: Early reports undercounted the dead. Why do disaster tolls keep changing?
basliklar: Why the Great Smog of London Was So Deadly
The Fog That Killed Thousands
sahneler: A thick yellow smog settled over London for five days.
Within days, thousands of people were killed by it.
The weather was unusually cold and windless.
Homes burned coal to stay warm.
An anticyclone trapped the smoke over the city.
Visibility dropped so low that buses stopped.
Later research put the death toll far higher than first reports.
It led to the Clean Air Act of 1956.

baslik: The Navy Blamed a Sailor. Scientists Found Another Cause
tetik: powder bags likely rammed too far and too fast
mekanizma: an overram compressing and igniting powder bags during loading
ders: the Navy expressed regret and the case became a lesson in investigation bias
yanilgi: The first investigation blamed a crew member. Independent testing pointed to an accidental overram.
tartisma: The Navy's conclusion was challenged by Sandia scientists. How do investigations avoid finding a scapegoat?
basliklar: What Really Caused the USS Iowa Explosion
The Turret Explosion and the Wrong Suspect
sahneler: During a fleet exercise, a gun turret on the battleship Iowa exploded.
Fire tore through the gunroom, and forty seven sailors were killed.
The Navy's first investigation blamed a sailor who died.
It claimed he caused the blast on purpose.
Families and Congress pushed back.
Sandia scientists found powder bags had likely been rammed too far and too fast.
An accidental overram could ignite them.
The Navy expressed regret but didn't apologize.

baslik: A Wrong Turn Put a Destroyer Under an Aircraft Carrier
sonuc: was cut in half by the carrier HMAS Melbourne
tetik: a turn across the carrier's bow in darkness
mekanizma: a conning officer misjudging relative position and turning into the carrier's path
ders: night formation manoeuvre procedures were examined after the collision
yanilgi: The destroyer didn't collide by chance. Its officer believed it was on the carrier's other side.
tartisma: Melbourne had cut another destroyer in half years earlier. Why do the same failures repeat?
basliklar: Why USS Frank E. Evans Was Cut in Half
The Destroyer That Turned the Wrong Way
sahneler: In darkness, an aircraft carrier sliced an American destroyer in two.
The bow sank in less than five minutes, and seventy four men were killed.
The ships were sailing without lights.
The destroyer was ordered to take up a rescue station.
Its officer thought the ship was on the carrier's other side.
It turned across the carrier's bow.
HMAS Melbourne had sunk another destroyer the same way before.
Night formation procedures came under scrutiny.

baslik: The Unexplained Turn That Sank a Destroyer
sonuc: sank after colliding with the carrier USS Wasp
tetik: a turn across the carrier's path at night
mekanizma: a destroyer attempting to cross ahead of a turning carrier and being struck amidships
ders: the Allied Navy Signal Book was changed after the inquiry
yanilgi: The safe option was simple: slow down. The destroyer tried to race ahead instead.
tartisma: An officer on the bridge warned of collision too late. When should juniors overrule the captain?
basliklar: Why USS Hobson Sank
The Destroyer That Raced Across a Carrier
sahneler: At night in the Atlantic, the carrier Wasp struck the destroyer Hobson.
It broke in two and sank quickly, and one hundred seventy six men were killed.
The carrier was turning to recover aircraft.
The usual move was to slow down and let it pass.
Hobson's captain tried to cross in front instead.
He ordered a hard left turn into the carrier's path.
An inquiry called it an unexplained left turn.
The Allied Navy Signal Book was changed.

baslik: Two Captains Assumed the Other Would Turn
sonuc: sank after a collision near Novorossiysk
tetik: a freighter holding course despite warnings
mekanizma: collision after both captains violated navigation rules and assumed the other would give way
ders: both captains were jailed and Soviet maritime safety came under scrutiny
yanilgi: The ships were in radio contact. Both sides assumed the collision wouldn't happen.
tartisma: Both captains got 15 years. Should both sides share equal blame?
basliklar: Why the Admiral Nakhimov Sank
The Collision Both Captains Saw Coming
sahneler: Near Novorossiysk, a bulk carrier rammed the Soviet liner Admiral Nakhimov.
It sank within minutes, and four hundred twenty three people died.
A pilot radioed a warning to the freighter.
The reply was: don't worry.
The freighter didn't slow or turn.
The liner's captain had gone to his cabin.
The officers exchanged radio calls, but it was too late.
Both captains were sentenced to fifteen years.

baslik: A Tanker's Anchor Hooked a Coast Guard Ship and Rolled It
sonuc: capsized after colliding with a tanker in Tampa Bay
tetik: both vessels failing to keep to their side of the channel
mekanizma: a tanker's ready anchor embedding in the hull and its chain pulling the tender over
ders: the investigation blamed both vessels and stressed signalling intentions in narrow channels
yanilgi: The collision alone didn't sink it. The tanker's anchor hooked the hull and dragged the ship over.
tartisma: No whistle signals were exchanged. How do two ships agree on who goes where?
basliklar: Why the USCGC Blackthorn Capsized
The Anchor That Rolled a Ship
sahneler: In Tampa Bay, a Coast Guard buoy tender collided with a tanker.
Within minutes it capsized, and twenty three crew were killed.
Neither ship kept to its side of the channel.
They didn't exchange whistle signals.
The tanker's anchor was ready to drop.
It embedded in the tender's hull.
The chain pulled the smaller ship onto its side.
Investigators blamed both ships for failing to signal their intentions.

baslik: The Rocket Skin Too Thin to Carry a Capsule
sonuc: broke up in flight a minute after launch
tetik: loads exceeding the thin skin below the capsule
mekanizma: buckling of the pressure-stabilized skin under combined drag, acceleration and bending loads
ders: NASA added doublers to the skin and made the trajectory shallower
yanilgi: Nobody saw the failure. Clouds hid the rocket, so engineers had to rebuild the story from the sea floor.
tartisma: Engineers objected to launching in bad weather. When should objections stop a launch?
basliklar: Why Mercury-Atlas 1 Failed
The Skin That Buckled at Max Q
soru: When should objections stop a launch?
sahneler: The first launch of a Mercury capsule on an Atlas rocket failed.
After fifty eight seconds, the rocket suddenly broke up.
Rain and clouds hid it from view.
Engineers had objected to launching in that weather.
Salvage crews recovered parts from the ocean floor.
The thin skin below the capsule had likely buckled.
Drag, acceleration, and bending loads were too much.
NASA added doublers to the skin and made the trajectory shallower.

baslik: The Rocket That Shook Like a Pogo Stick
sonuc: shook violently and lost engines on its test flight
tetik: pogo oscillations from feed line resonance
mekanizma: thrust fluctuations resonating with propellant lines and the vehicle structure
ders: pogo suppression was added before the Saturn V carried crews
yanilgi: The shaking wasn't random. Engine, pipes, and structure resonated like an organ pipe and a tuning fork.
tartisma: The next Saturn V carried astronauts to the Moon. Was one fix enough to trust it?
basliklar: Why Apollo 6 Nearly Shook Itself Apart
The Pogo Oscillation That Threatened Apollo
hook: It shook like a pogo stick
sahneler: Two minutes after launch, the Saturn V on Apollo 6 began to shake.
Suddenly the vibrations exceeded its design limits.
Engine thrust always fluctuates slightly.
The fuel lines had their own resonance, like an organ pipe.
The structure vibrated like a tuning fork.
Later, engine lines ruptured and two engines shut down early.
A wiring error shut down the second one.
Pogo suppression was added before crews flew.
